Definition: from G3844 and G5342 (including its alternate forms); to bear along or aside, i.e. carry off (literally or figuratively); by implication, to avert:--remove, take away.
BiblicalUsage: Paraphero means to carry aside, to take away. In Gethsemane Jesus prays, Father, if thou be willing, remove this cup from me, in Luke 22:42 and Mark 14:36. Hebrews 13:9 warns believers not to be carried about with strange doctrines, and Jude 1:12 calls false teachers clouds carried about of winds, with no water in them.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the same word holds both the prayer of Gethsemane and the warning against drifting: the cup could be removed, but Jesus drank it, and I must not let strange teaching carry me where He did not go. I hold that the cup He drank is the reason my drifting is forgiven, and the doctrine that carries me must be the one that keeps me at His cross.
